extracted.intended_audience: lessees, grant holders, and their consultants/attorneys preparing BOEM SAP, COP, GAP, and related submissions for OCS renewable energy (offshore wind) projects
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory criteria for preparing Site Assessment Plans (SAPs), Construction and Operations Plans (COPs), General Activities Plans (GAPs), and related reports and demonstrations required by BOEM under proposed amendments to 30 CFR Part 585.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial assurance release and reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may release a lessee's or grant holder's financial assurance whenever BOEM determines that it is no longer needed (including if assurance ceased prior to accrual of any decommissioning obligation or was erroneously assessed). BOEM may require reinstatement of a financial assurance instrument as if no cancellation occurred if an obligor's payment is rescinded due to insolvency or bankruptcy, or if the responsible party's representation that it discharged obligations was materially false when the bond was cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed change responds to lessee requests to depart from the 7-year post-lease financial assurance hold; adapts language from oil and gas regs (30 CFR 556.906(e)) to protect U.S. taxpayer. Reinstatement authority applies where payments are rescinded or representations were materially false.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology: use 'financial assurance' instead of 'bond'
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical substitution of the phrase 'financial assurance' for the word 'bond' in relevant provisions (e.g., §585.535).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an editorial/technical correction to better reflect the range of acceptable instruments and avoid implying only bonds are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP requirement limited to engineered foundations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under proposed §585.600(a)(1), SAPs would be required only for site assessment activities involving an 'engineered foundation,' exempting floating site assessment facilities (e.g., met buoys) from the SAP requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change intended to exempt floating site assessment facilities; BOEM seeks comment on whether the definition of 'engineered foundation' is appropriate or whether a different term should be used to determine SAP applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'engineered foundation'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term would include met towers or other structures installed using a fixed-bottom foundation requiring professional engineering design and assessment of sediment, meteorological, and oceanographic condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lessee unsure whether their facility triggers the SAP requirement, they are encouraged to consult BOEM early. Example: industry-standard met buoy using gravity anchor would not require a SAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM discretion to waive certain plan information or analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may waive certain information or analysis requirements in a proposed plan if the applicant demonstrates that the information is known to BOEM, the relevant resource is not present or affected, or the information is not needed or required by a State's coastal management program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language modeled on 30 CFR 550.201(c); grants BOEM flexibility to tailor plan requirements to unique proposal elements without issuing regulatory departures under §585.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP timing: flexible submittal period
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessees and grant holders may submit a SAP anytime during the life of the lease or grant, but must submit a SAP before conducting any activities that require a SAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed removal of requirement to submit SAP before or within 12 months of lease/grant issuance to provide flexibility; rationale includes instances where COP filed prior to SAP or additional data collection after COP.

rubrics_metrics.name: COP and GAP timing revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under proposed rule, a COP is due within 5 years of the lease effective date. The 12-month period for GAP submittal starts at the effective date of the limited lease or grant (consistent with §585.303(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions align COP/GAP timing with proposed lease period changes in §585.235/§585.236.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping expansion to include lease/grant compliance and SMS
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessees and grant holders would be required to retain records relating to lease or grant compliance, including Safety Management System (SMS) requirements, not just data/information related to plan compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change proposed to ensure a fuller compliance record is available to monitor trends and ensure safety and SMS effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP content: allowance of Project Design Envelope (PDE) and use of parameter ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: A lessee may use a PDE in its SAP; project-specific information may be provided as a range of parameters, but any range must provide both a minimum and a maximum value (e.g., not simply 'at least 200 turbines').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple foundation types proposed, lessee must describe which type is expected to have greatest impact on each resource. Paragraph (a)(5) allows proposing a range of potential locations and an indicative layout in lieu of a location plat. Paragraph (a)(6) clarifies only preliminary design information is required; detailed drawings may be submitted with FDR if project is complex/significant under §585.613(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: CVA nomination delinked; project verification strategy required
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of requiring a CVA nomination with SAP or COP, a lessee would submit a 'project verification strategy' describing the lessee's plan for complying with CVA regulations; a CVA can be nominated before or after SAP/COP submittal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delinking intended to allow benefit of CVA review as early as feasible. For SAPs, strategy should analyze whether the project should be considered complex or significant and describe approach to comply with proposed subpart H requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP processing and resubmission timing (resubmission within reasonable time)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM proposes to clarify that SAP resubmission must occur within a reasonable time and make analogous changes to COP and GAP provisions on resubmission and processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmonizes timing and actions across SAP/COP/GAP; proposed changes include cross-references to analogous COP/GAP requirements (§§585.628 and 585.648).

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP/COP/GAP information and certifications to assist NEPA and other laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifications to informational requirements include: water quality information explicitly includes vessel discharges; archaeological resources explicitly include all types of historic properties (NHPA); coastal and marine uses explicitly include fisheries assessments and navigational safety risk assessments, the latter to be submitted to USCG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also replaces phrase 'relevant laws' with 'applicable laws' for clarity and reorganizes paragraphing to improve clarity. These clarifications are consistent with BOEM's present expectations and should not create added burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: CZMA Federal consistency: when a consistency certification is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessees need submit a CZMA consistency certification for their SAPs under 15 CFR part 930, subpart E only if BOEM has not previously submitted a consistency determination to that State under subpart C that covered the proposed site assessment activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM and NOAA expect most review to occur via BOEM's subpart C consistency determination at lease sale stage; separate CZMA reviews for SAP/GAP/COP should be rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: COP submission to States for Federal consistency after NEPA draft availability
rubrics_metrics.description: After all COP information requirements are met and after the appropriate environmental assessment or draft EIS has been published, the lessee/grant holder must submit COP consistency certification and associated data to applicable State CZMA agencies through BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shifts the 'active application' date for COP under 15 CFR 930.51(f) such that the CZMA review period starts on the date BOEM issues notice of availability for the draft NEPA analysis rather than the date of the NOI to publish a draft NEPA analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: COP contents: use of PDE; project verification strategy instead of CVA nomination
rubrics_metrics.description: A lessee may use a PDE in its COP; requirement to submit a CVA nomination with the COP replaced by requirement to submit a project verification strategy describing compliance with CVA regs (§§585.705–585.714).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows flexibility to nominate and for BOEM to approve CVA either before or after COP submittal. Strategy should describe approach to verification and whether project is complex/significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation and renaming of geological/geotechnical survey requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Merge 'shallow hazards', 'geological', 'geotechnical', and 'site investigation' survey requirements into 'geological and geotechnical' survey requirements (§585.626(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change clarifies overlap and reduces redundancy; shallow hazards are part of geological and geotechnical surveys rather than a separate survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance-based standards for geophysical and geotechnical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace prescriptive requirements (e.g., minimum number/depth of borings) with performance-based standards focused on sufficiency of information regarding geological site conditions BOEM needs to review a COP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geophysical data must 'define the geological conditions of the site's seabed that could impact, or be impacted by, the proposed project.' Geotechnical data must 'ground truth the geophysical surveys; support development of a geological model; assess potential geological hazards that could impact the proposed project; and provide geotechnical data for preliminary design of the facility, including type and approximate dimensions of the foundation.' BOEM will continue sufficiency review after COP receipt and notify lessee of additional outstanding info prior to completing review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of mandatory in situ borings requirement (with compensation via performance standards/FDR submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed elimination of the existing obligation to submit results of adequate in situ testing, boring, and sampling at each foundation location and a minimum of one deep boring at each project edge; instead require geophysical and geotechnical data of sufficient quality and, where detailed geotechnical surveys are required for engineering, submission with the FDR (§585.701).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change intended to provide flexibility and respond to lessee concerns while preserving quality of geotechnical data reviewed before construction. Geophysical surveys still must identify all relevant shallow hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing flexibility for archaeological surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow certain detailed subsea archaeological surveys to be submitted with the FDR under proposed §585.701(a)(11) rather than at COP submittal; deferral permitted on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral may create additional permitting and business risk for lessee; required reports include information on all historic properties listed or eligible for listing on the National Register per NHPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desktop oceanographic and meteorological data requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Require desktop data on oceanographic and meteorological conditions sufficient to 'support preliminary design of the facility and support the analysis of wake effects, sediment mobility and scour, and navigational risks' (§585.626(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This complements existing condition/hazard data requirements and is intended to better inform modeling, design, and environmental reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil Spill Response Plan (OSRP) statutory standard and cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a lessee to submit an OSRP 'in compliance with 33 U.S.C. 1321, including information identified in 30 CFR part 254 that is applicable to your activities' rather than cross-referencing 30 CFR part 254 alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change reflects that 30 CFR part 254 applies only to OCS oil & gas activities; statutory provision 33 U.S.C. 1321 covers spills beyond oil & gas and gives flexibility to craft OSRPs commensurate with estimated worst-case discharge for renewable facilities. BOEM (with BSEE) intends to issue guidance on recommended OSRP contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project easement width and off-lease area flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may issue project easements of 'sufficient off-lease area to accommodate potential changes at the design and installation phases' for cables, pipelines, and appurtenances; lessees may relinquish unused portions after construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: precise cable routes may not be known at COP approval; larger easements accommodate uncertainty and reduce need for amendments. Larger easement increases rental fees per §585.507. Project easements subject to same conditions as ROWs/RUEs under §585.302(b) allowing U.S. to grant overlapping rights to others that do not unreasonably interfere.

rubrics_metrics.name: COP revision triggers and incorporation of PDE to scale revision threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revisions eliminate redundant verbiage about changes that trigger COP revision and explicitly incorporate the PDE concept (a 'range' of facility locations) so thresholds to trigger COP revision can be proportionate to project magnitude; BOEM seeks comment on what threshold should trigger revisions for changes in position/layout of bottom disturbances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation of PDE reduces prescriptiveness and allows thresholds to be proportional to magnitude of changes; intended to reduce unnecessary COP revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement of commercial operations: verification timing and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial operations may commence 30 calendar days after BOEM deems submitted the final project verification report (as described in proposed §§585.704 and 585.708(a)(5)), provided BOEM has not notified the lessee of objections within that time and BOEM has confirmed receipt of critical safety systems commissioning records (§585.637).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies consistency with §585.708(a)(5)(ii) and replaces 'certification' with 'verification'; moves requirement to notify BOEM within 10 business days of starting commercial operations into §585.637. BOEM deems submissions 'submitted' for purposes of the 30-day clock; ensures BOEM is in possession of complete and accurate submissions prior to limited review period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition change: electricity generation for testing excluded from 'commercial operations' under conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed edit to exclude generation of electricity needed for preparation of the final FIR or generation for testing purposes from the definition of 'commercial operations' provided such electricity is not sold on a commercial basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responds to practical instances of generation/distribution during testing activities prior to required reports; seeks comment on change to definition of commercial activities/operations (§585.112).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decommissioning timing aligned to allow application up to 2 years before lease expiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed subpart J contemplates initiation of the decommissioning process by submitting a decommissioning application as much as 2 years before lease expiration; corresponding edits proposed in SAP/COP/GAP completion sections for consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions intended to harmonize timing across sections (§§585.618, 585.638, 585.905, 585.906).

rubrics_metrics.name: GAP content and administrative consistency with SAP/COP
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed changes to GAPs align content and informational clarifications with those proposed for SAPs and COPs (e.g., elimination of paper copy requirement; consistency in informational certifications to assist NEPA and other applicable laws).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes technical edits ensuring consistency with §585.303(a) on due date and removal of redundant text; proposed elimination of paper copies consistent with §585.110.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of paper copy requirement for plan submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed elimination of paper copy requirements for SAP, COP, and GAP submittals (consistent with proposed changes to §585.110).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernizes submission process and reduces administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM sufficiency review after COP receipt and notice of additional information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will continue to perform a sufficiency review after receipt of a COP and will notify the lessee of any additional outstanding information requirements prior to completing the COP review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures BOEM has sufficient information to conduct environmental analyses and interagency consultations; complements move to performance-based data requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR/FIR staged submittal flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM has authority to allow lessees to submit Facility Design Reports (FDRs) and Fabrication and Installation Reports (FIRs) for BOEM review by stage or component so lessees may commence fabrication or construction of project components while other aspects remain under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms flexibility in certain circumstances to proceed with staged fabrication/installation; described in section V.D.3(b) entitled 'Staged Submittal of the Facility Design Report and Fabrication and Installation Report.'
